title: Zero-order-hold discretization
goal:
Implement Equation 4 from Section 2 for a diagonal $A$ and an input-dependent step size, in the shapes of Algorithm 2 (Section 3.2): $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ and $\bar{B} = (\Delta A)^{-1}(\exp(\Delta A) - I)\cdot \Delta B$.

Write `discretize(delta, A, B)`:

- `delta` has shape `(L, D)`, one step size per time step and channel.
- `A` has shape `(D, N)`. Each row holds the diagonal of one channel's $N \times N$ matrix, so every entry is a nonzero negative number.
- `B` has shape `(L, N)`, one input matrix per time step, shared by all channels.
- Return `(A_bar, B_bar)`, both with shape `(L, D, N)`.

Because $A$ is diagonal, Equation 4 is an elementwise formula: $\bar{A}_{t,d,n} = \exp(\Delta_{t,d} A_{d,n})$ and $\bar{B}_{t,d,n} = \frac{\bar{A}_{t,d,n} - 1}{A_{d,n}} B_{t,n}$.
hints: Broadcast with `delta[:, :, None] * A[None, :, :]`. The product has shape `(L, D, N)`.
In $(\Delta A)^{-1}(\exp(\Delta A) - I)\cdot \Delta B$ the two factors of $\Delta$ cancel. What remains is $(\bar{A} - 1) / A$ times $B$.
`np.expm1(x)` computes `exp(x) - 1` without losing precision when `x` is close to 0.
`B` has no channel axis. Add one with `B[:, None, :]` so it broadcasts against `(L, D, N)`.
